brief: Goldman Delta One desk head Rich Privorotsky argues micro is getting more encouraging while macro is getting harder. Net-net he calls the August payrolls report firmer, with unemployment at 4.1%, so the front end repriced despite seasonal payback excuses and September hike odds moved back toward 60%. Friday's CPI is the binary event: a benign print gives the Committee room to wait, a hot core probably solidifies a September hike, and a mechanical reprice would take the roughly 60bps of tightening priced through year-end to 75. Strong nominal growth offsets that, so equities can stay resilient. Oil is the biggest macro problem, with Brent near $97, Hormuz tanker traffic at its lowest since May, the SPR at 287 million barrels and Iran threatening a formal restricted zone, though he sees scope for a diplomatic headline because pressure on both sides is becoming acute. On micro, Astra is materially more token-efficient on agentic workloads, cutting cost per completed task, which he reads as supporting more usage and infrastructure spend, with SoftBank up 10% and Kospi up 4-5%. The AfD's 43.8% in Saxony-Anhalt was expected. France is the one he would trade, watching OATs into budget season. Institutional positioning is light.
